# Equation of state and thermodynamic functions {#sec-ch03}

This chapter describes the thermodynamic state of a kintera mixture and the functions that evaluate it: the species
order and the two state vectors (mole fractions in `ThermoX`, mass fractions in `ThermoY`); the ideal-gas equation
of state with its inversions; the heat capacities and internal energies, in the constant-heat-capacity baseline and
in the two opt-in models for temperature-dependent gases; the reference state at which the card gives its data and
the latent heat that follows from it; the entropy of gases and condensates, where the condensate entropy is derived
from the saturation curve; the saturation ratio as a diagnostic; and the moist adiabatic extrapolation that steps a
parcel in pressure or height while conserving its entropy. The phase-equilibrium solvers that the entropy and the
adiabat depend on are the subject of @sec-ch04; the saturation-pressure curves themselves belong to @sec-ch02. All
formulas are written for the species indices and symbols defined in @sec-ch03-species-state, and every scheme ends
with an executable check under `src/kintera_report/ch03/checks/` whose output is committed next to it.

### Summary

Every thermodynamic routine of kintera works on a list of species that is split into two groups: the gases first,
then the condensates. The list is read once from the `species` block of the YAML card, every reaction of the card
sorts its participants into one of the two groups, and from then on the position of a species in the list is its
index everywhere: in the mole-fraction vector of `ThermoX`, in the mass-fraction vector of `ThermoY`, in the
stoichiometric matrix and in the outputs of the saturation solvers of @sec-ch04. This section fixes that ordering,
the two state vectors and the conversions between them, because every later formula in this chapter and in
@sec-ch04 is written in those indices.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Define the species order (gases, then condensates), the mole-fraction state $x_i$ of `ThermoX` and the
mass-fraction state $y_i$ of `ThermoY`, and the conversions between them; the defining relation is
@eq-ch03-species-state-x-from-y.

**Data.** `species` entries of the card with `name`, `composition`, optional `phase`, `cv_R`, `u0_R`, `s0_R`; in
memory `vapor_ids`, `cloud_ids`, `mu` [$\mathrm{kg\,mol^{-1}}$]; $x_i$ on the last tensor axis, $y_i$ on the first.

**Placement.** At construction of `ThermoOptions` (card reading) and of `ThermoX` or `ThermoY` (`reset`); the
conversions run whenever a host code calls `compute` with one of the keys of @tbl-ch03-species-state-code.

**Activation.** Always; `phase: gas|liquid|solid` is optional and only the explicit way to put an inert gas or a gaseous
reaction product into the gas group.

**Guarantee / limits.** The conversions are exact algebra, closed to round-off; a card whose phases contradict its
reactions is refused at load.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `test_thermo` round trips on CPU and CUDA, float and double.
:::

Local symbols of this section, used throughout the chapter: $N$ species of which $N_{\mathrm g}$ are gases and
$N_{\mathrm c} = N - N_{\mathrm g}$ condensates, indexed by $i = 0, \dots, N-1$ in the order above (species $0$ is the
first gas, the reference species of the mass basis); $x_i$ the mole fraction of species $i$ among all species, gas and
condensed [-]; $y_i$ its mass fraction [-]; $c_i$ its molar concentration [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $\rho_i$ its
partial density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$] and $\rho = \sum_i \rho_i$ the total density; $M_i$ its molar mass
[$\mathrm{kg\,mol^{-1}}$]; $x_{\mathrm g} = \sum_{i < N_{\mathrm g}} x_i$ the gas share of the moles and
$c_{\mathrm g} = \sum_{i < N_{\mathrm g}} c_i$ the gas concentration. None of these is in the shared notation table
yet; they are proposed to the editor. The internal name of the mole basis is `ThermoX` and of the
mass basis `ThermoY`; the code calls the gas group `vapor` and the condensate group `cloud`.

### Derivation

The card lists species by name and elemental composition. The molar mass $M_i$ is the composition-weighted sum of the
element masses, and the optional caloric entries `cv_R`, `u0_R` and `s0_R` are stored as they are read (their meaning
is the subject of @sec-ch03-caloric and @sec-ch03-reference-state). A species that is named nowhere else is a gas
only if the card says `phase: gas`; otherwise the groups are inferred from the reactions: every nucleation reactant is
a gas, every nucleation product without `phase: gas` is a condensate, and the first species of the card is a gas (the
reference species). Within each group the species keep the card order. The result is the species vector of the whole
chapter,
$$
(\underbrace{x_0, x_1, \dots, x_{N_{\mathrm g}-1}}_{\text{gases}},\;
 \underbrace{x_{N_{\mathrm g}}, \dots, x_{N-1}}_{\text{condensates}}),
$$
and no routine infers an index from the text of a reaction.

`ThermoX` keeps mole fractions of *all* species, so that $\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} x_i = 1$ and the condensates are counted
in the moles; `ThermoY` keeps the mass fractions $y_1, \dots, y_{N-1}$ of every species except the reference species,
whose mass fraction is $y_0 = 1 - \sum_{i \ge 1} y_i$. The two are related through the molar masses. With
$y_i = x_i M_i / \sum_k x_k M_k$, dividing numerator and denominator by $M_0$ and eliminating $x_0 = 1 - \sum_{k\ge1}
x_k$ gives, for $i \ge 1$,
$$
x_i = \frac{y_i\,M_0/M_i}{1 + \sum_{k \ge 1} y_k\,(M_0/M_k - 1)}, \qquad x_0 = 1 - \sum_{i \ge 1} x_i,
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-x-from-y}
which is the form the code evaluates: @eq-ch03-species-state-x-from-y
is computed in `ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_xfrac` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_xfrac >}}),
with `inv_mu` holding $1/M_i$ and `mud` the reference mass $M_0$. The inverse map is the definition itself,
$$
y_i = \frac{x_i M_i}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} x_k M_k}, \qquad i = 1, \dots, N-1,
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-y-from-x}
and @eq-ch03-species-state-y-from-x is computed in `ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_yfrac`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_yfrac >}}). That the two are inverses is checked
symbolically and numerically (check lines `[C1]` and `[C2]` of `species_state_check.py`).

The mass basis also needs the partial densities. Given the total density $\rho$ and the mass fractions,
$$
\rho_0 = \rho\,\Bigl(1 - \sum_{i \ge 1} y_i\Bigr), \qquad \rho_i = \rho\,y_i \quad (i \ge 1),
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-ivol}
and @eq-ch03-species-state-ivol is computed in `ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_ivol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_ivol >}}); the code calls the vector of partial densities
`ivol`. Its inverse $y_i = \rho_i / \sum_k \rho_k$ is `ThermoYImpl::_ivol_to_yfrac`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_ivol_to_yfrac >}}), and the molar concentrations follow as
$c_i = \rho_i / M_i$ wherever a caloric function needs them (`[C3]`).

The mole basis needs concentrations from $(T, p, x)$. For an ideal gas the gas-only mole fractions
$x_i / x_{\mathrm g}$ are the partial-pressure fractions, so
$$
c_i = \frac{x_i}{x_{\mathrm g}}\,\frac{p}{\mathcal R\,T} \quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}), \qquad
c_i = c_0\,\frac{x_i}{x_0} \quad (i \ge N_{\mathrm g}),
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-conc}
where the condensates are scaled from the reference gas so that the mole ratios of the input are kept.
@eq-ch03-species-state-conc is computed in `ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc >}}), whose Newton loop on the compressibility factor
is the subject of @sec-ch03-eos; with the ideal-gas factor it is the closed form above (`[C4]`). The reverse step, the
total density from concentrations, is $\rho = \sum_i c_i M_i$ in `ThermoXImpl::_conc_to_dens`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_conc_to_dens >}}).

Everything in this section is exact algebra; the only approximation is the ideal-gas relation in
@eq-ch03-species-state-conc, whose generalisation is @sec-ch03-eos. The check `species_state_check.py` verifies the
closed forms symbolically and the round trips to round-off.

### Numerical method

There is no iteration here. The two state vectors differ in layout as well as in basis, and the layout is what a host
code has to get right: `ThermoX` stores $x_i$ on the *last* tensor axis, shape $(\dots, 1 + n_y)$ with
$n_y = N - 1$, while `ThermoY` stores $y_i$ on the *first* axis, shape $(n_y, \dots)$, so that a hydrodynamic code
can hand over its tracer array without a copy. @fig-ch03-species-state-layout shows both for the species of
`tests/jupiter.yaml` (four gases, three condensates). Every conversion permutes the species axis to the front,
operates, and permutes back; the permutation is a view, not a copy.

The species groups are decided once, at option construction, by `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}): it starts the gas set with the
first species of the card, adds the reactants and products of every nucleation, coagulation and evaporation reaction
through `add_to_vapor_cloud` ({{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp add_to_vapor_cloud >}}), then adds every species
with an explicit `phase`, refuses a species that would end up in both groups, sorts each group by card index and
copies the caloric data in that order. A `ThermoX` or `ThermoY` built from the options then calls
`check_dimensions` ({{< code src/species.cpp check_dimensions >}}) in its `reset` to make sure every per-species array
has exactly $N$ entries; the arrays an object built without a card may lack are filled with no-op defaults by
`populate_thermo` ({{< code src/species.cpp populate_thermo >}}).

Walk-through, in the order a host code meets it:

1. Load the card. `init_species_from_yaml` ({{< code src/species.cpp init_species_from_yaml overload=2 >}}) fills
   the process-global registry: names, phases, molar masses, `cv_R` (default $5/2$), `u0_R` (default 0), `s0_R`
   (default 0) and the NASA-9 record if the name is in the bundled database. A `phase` other than `gas`, `liquid` or
   `solid` is refused. The registry is global, which is why the kintera tests that load several cards run each in its
   own interpreter.
2. Build the options. `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml` returns a null pointer when the card has no `reference-state`
   block; otherwise it reads the block (@sec-ch03-reference-state), the `dynamics/equation-of-state`
   block of @sec-ch03-eos and the reactions, and forms the two groups as described above. Three errors a user can
   hit here:
   `Gas species classified as cloud`, `Condensed species classified as gas` and
   `Conflicting gas/cloud classification`, each naming the species.
3. Build the module. `ThermoY` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}) registers the buffers
   `inv_mu` ($1/M_i$), `cv0`, `u0` and `stoich`; `ThermoX` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::reset >}})
   registers `mu` and `stoich`. Both refuse a nucleation reaction with a condensed reactant or without a condensed
   product.
4. Convert. `ThermoYImpl::compute` and `ThermoXImpl::compute` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::compute >}})
   dispatch on the key string; an unknown key throws `Unknown abbreviation`, and `Y->X`, `X->Y`, `V->Y`, `DY->V` check
   that the species axis has length $N$ or $N - 1$ (`mass fraction size mismatch`).

A minimal card and the conversions it enables, in the public Python API (@sec-ch11):

```python
import torch
from kintera import ThermoOptions, ThermoX, ThermoY
# species: dry, H2O, NH3, H2S | H2O(l), NH3(s), NH4SH(s)
op = ThermoOptions.from_yaml("tests/jupiter.yaml")
tx, ty = ThermoX(op), ThermoY(op)
yfrac = torch.full((6, 2, 3), 0.01, dtype=torch.float64)  # (n_y, ...)
xfrac = ty.compute("Y->X", [yfrac])                     # (..., 1 + n_y)
yback = tx.compute("X->Y", [xfrac])                     # round trip
```

### Limits

- The species registry is process-global: loading a second card with a different `species` list replaces it, and an
  options object built before the reload keeps its own copy of names and masses but not of the registry. Two cards in
  one process with different species are not a tested configuration (the kintera tests isolate them in subprocesses).
- The implicit classification (first species and nucleation reactants are gases) is the legacy path; a card with a
  gaseous reaction product (@sec-ch04) or an inert gas that appears in no reaction must say `phase: gas`,
  or that species is left out of the gas group silently (an inert gas) or refused (a product).
- `ThermoX` counts condensates in the mole fractions, so $x_i$ is not a gas-only mixing ratio and the `x_` columns of
  the examples must be read that way; `ThermoY` carries no explicit entry for the reference species, so a negative
  remainder $1 - \sum_{i\ge1} y_i$ is not detected here (it surfaces as a negative gas concentration in
  @sec-ch04).
- Not measured: the cost of the axis permutations on CUDA for large tracer arrays.

### Summary

The pressure of a kintera mixture is the ideal-gas pressure of its gases: condensates occupy no volume and exert no
pressure, and the gas species share the volume. The code writes this with a per-species compressibility factor $z_i$
in front of each gas concentration, so that a non-ideal gas could be added through a user function; at the code pin
no such function is registered, and $z_i = 1$ for every gas. This section states the equation of state, the three
inversions the host codes use (pressure from temperature, temperature from pressure, and concentrations from mole
fractions) and why two of them are Newton loops that take exactly one step for an ideal gas.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $p = \mathcal R\,T\sum_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} z_i c_i$, @eq-ch03-eos-pressure, and its inversions.

**Data.** In: $T$ [K] or $p$ [Pa] with the partial densities (`ThermoY`) or the mole fractions (`ThermoX`); out: the
missing one, or the concentrations $c_i$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$].

**Placement.** `compute` keys `VT->P`, `PV->T` (`ThermoY`) and `TPX->V` (`ThermoX`); the saturation solvers call
`VT->P` for their initial guess.

**Activation.** Always. `dynamics/equation-of-state` sets `max-iter` (default 10) and `ftol` (default $10^{-6}$) for the
Newton loops; `gas_floor` ($10^{-20}\,\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$, not a card key) guards the division by the gas total.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact for an ideal gas (one Newton step); the damping argument for $z_i \ne 1$ is given but
untested, since no $z_i \ne 1$ exists at the pin.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `DeviceTest.thermo_y` and `DeviceTest.eng_pres` close the `VT->P`/`PV->T` loop to
$10^{-4}$.
:::

Local symbols: $z_i$ the compressibility factor of gas $i$ [-] (`czh`), $z_{i,c} = \partial z_i/\partial c_i$ (`czh_ddC`)
and $z_{i,T} = \partial z_i/\partial T$; $\hat c_{v,i} = c_{v,i}/\mathcal R$ and $\hat c_{p,i} = c_{p,i}/\mathcal R$
the dimensionless molar heat capacities (`cv_R`, `cp_R`); $K_{\max}$ the iteration cap (`max-iter`) and
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ the relative stopping tolerance (`ftol`). The species symbols are those of
@sec-ch03-species-state.

### Derivation

Each gas species obeys $p_i = z_i(T, c_i)\,c_i\,\mathcal R\,T$ and the condensates contribute nothing, so the total
pressure is
$$
p = \mathcal R\,T \sum_{i=0}^{N_{\mathrm g}-1} z_i(T, c_i)\,c_i .
$$ {#eq-ch03-eos-pressure}
@eq-ch03-eos-pressure is computed in `ThermoYImpl::_temp_to_pres`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_temp_to_pres >}}), which converts the partial densities to
concentrations with `inv_mu` and evaluates $z_i$ through `eval_czh` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_czh >}}).
`eval_czh` fills the gas entries with $1$ and then calls the per-species function named in `czh`; at the pin the
registry of two-argument user functions is empty ({{< code src/func_table.cpp func2_names >}}), so every `czh` entry is
the empty string and $z_i \equiv 1$ (`[C1]` of `eos_check.py`).

The inverse problem, $T$ from $p$ and the partial densities, is the root of
$$
f(T) = T \sum_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} z_i(T, c_i)\,c_i - \frac{p}{\mathcal R} = 0 .
$$ {#eq-ch03-eos-ftemp}
Its exact slope is $f'(T) = \sum_i (z_i + T z_{i,T})\,c_i$. The code does not evaluate $z_{i,T}$; it divides by
$\sum_i (\hat c_{p,i} - \hat c_{v,i})\,c_i$ instead and takes the step
$$
T \leftarrow T - \frac{f(T)}{\sum_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} (\hat c_{p,i} - \hat c_{v,i})\,c_i},
\qquad T^{(0)} = \frac{p}{\mathcal R \sum_i c_i} .
$$ {#eq-ch03-eos-newton-t}
@eq-ch03-eos-newton-t is computed in `ThermoYImpl::_pres_to_temp`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_pres_to_temp >}}). Why this denominator is safe: for a gas whose
compressibility depends on $T$ and $c$, the Mayer relation reads $\hat c_p - \hat c_v = (z + T z_T)^2 / (z + c\,z_c)$,
and with $z_T \ge 0$, $z_c \le 0$ (a dissociating gas) that is at least the exact slope $z + T z_T$, so the step is
never longer than the Newton step: a damped Newton iteration that cannot overshoot the root (`[C3]`). For an ideal gas
$\hat c_p - \hat c_v = 1$, $f'(T) = \sum c_i$, and the starting guess $T^{(0)}$ is already the root, so $f(T^{(0)}) = 0$
and the loop exits after its first pass (`[C2]`). The sign of the step matters: $f$ increases with $T$, so the
correction is subtracted.

The third inversion gives concentrations from $(T, p, x)$. For gases, @eq-ch03-eos-pressure with
$p_i = p\,x_i/x_{\mathrm g}$ is the fixed-point problem $z_i(T, c_i)\,c_i = c_i^{\mathrm{id}}$ with the ideal value
$c_i^{\mathrm{id}} = x_i p / (x_{\mathrm g}\mathcal R T)$ of @eq-ch03-species-state-conc, solved per species by
$$
c_i \leftarrow c_i + \frac{c_i^{\mathrm{id}} - z_i c_i}{z_{i,c}\,c_i + z_i}, \qquad c_i^{(0)} = c_i^{\mathrm{id}} .
$$ {#eq-ch03-eos-newton-c}
@eq-ch03-eos-newton-c is computed in `ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc >}}) with $z_{i,c}$ from `eval_czh_ddC`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_czh_ddC >}}); with $z_i = 1$, $z_{i,c} = 0$ the update is zero at the start
and the loop again exits after one pass (`[C4]`). The condensate concentrations follow from the reference gas,
$c_i = c_0 x_i / x_0$.

Nothing is truncated for an ideal gas: all three relations are closed forms and the loops reproduce them to
round-off. For $z_i \ne 1$ the two Newton loops stop when the largest relative change of the unknown falls below
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ or after $K_{\max}$ passes, with a warning in the second case; the damping makes the
temperature loop monotone but the convergence order for $z_i \ne 1$ is not established here, because no such $z_i$
exists at the pin. The executable check is `eos_check.py` (`[C1]` to `[C5]`).

### Numerical method

@fig-ch03-eos-conversions places the three inversions among the other conversion keys of the two modules. Each key
is one call; the solid arrows are closed forms and the dashed ones are the loops of this section and of
@sec-ch03-caloric and @sec-ch03-entropy. All keys act element-wise over the leading (cell) axes of the tensors, so a
column, a plane or a whole grid is one call; the stopping test of a loop is the *maximum* relative change over all
cells, so one slowly converging cell makes every cell iterate.

($z_i$, $z_{i,c}$, or the heat capacities) on the current iterate for all cells at once; the update is applied in

The loop variable $X$ is $T$ in `PV->T` and $c_i$ in `TPX->V`. Reaching $K_{\max}$ prints a warning
(`max iterations reached`) and returns the last iterate; `TPX->V` additionally writes the offending inputs to a
`.pt` file named after the time stamp, which is the one side effect on disk in this chapter. The gas concentrations
are floored at `gas_floor` before the division by their sum, so a cell without any gas returns a finite (and
meaningless) temperature instead of a division by zero (`[C5]`).

### Summary

The energy of a kintera parcel is the sum over species of a molar internal energy that is, by default, linear in
temperature: each species carries one dimensionless heat capacity `cv_R` and one energy offset. That baseline is
what the saturation solvers of @sec-ch04 and the hydrodynamic hosts assume, and it is exact for a mixture of
calorically perfect gases and incompressible condensates. Two opt-in models replace the constant heat capacity of
individual gases by a temperature-dependent one, for the cases where the baseline is visibly wrong: the NASA-9
polynomial fits for any species that has a record in the bundled database, and a parameter-free rotational partition
function for molecular hydrogen, whose heat capacity drops from $7/2\,\mathcal R$ to $5/2\,\mathcal R$ below about
$150\,\mathrm K$ and shows the ortho-para conversion peak near $50\,\mathrm K$. This section gives the three models,
the enthalpy and heat capacity at constant pressure that follow from them, and the inversion from energy to temperature.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $u_i(T)$, $c_{v,i}(T)$, $c_{p,i}(T)$ and $h_i(T)$ per species, @eq-ch03-caloric-u-baseline, and the
volumetric sums $U = \sum_i c_i u_i$, $C_V$, $C_p$, $H$.

**Data.** In: $T$ [K] and the concentrations $c_i$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; out: molar quantities divided by
$\mathcal R$ (`*_R`, in K or dimensionless) and the volumetric sums in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and
$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$.

**Placement.** `compute` keys `VT->cv`, `VT->U`, `VU->T` (`ThermoY`) and `TV->cp`, `TV->H` (`ThermoX`); inside every
saturation solve and adiabat step.

**Activation.** Baseline always, from the card's per-species `cv_R` (default $5/2$). `reference-state:
{use-nasa9-cp: true}` switches species with a NASA-9 record to the polynomial; `use-h2-cp: true` switches the species
named `H2` to the rotor, with `h2-cp-mode: equilibrium` (default) or `normal`. Both default to off.

**Guarantee / limits.** Baseline exact for constant heat capacities; both opt-in models join the baseline
continuously at $T_0 = 300\,\mathrm K$ and leave the entropy on the baseline.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `test_nasa9_cp.py` (rtol $10^{-10}$), `test_h2_cp.py` ($2\times10^{-3}$).
:::

Local symbols: $u_i, h_i, s_i$ the molar internal energy, enthalpy and entropy of species $i$ [$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$,
$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$]; $\hat u_i = u_i/\mathcal R$ [K] and likewise $\hat h_i$, $\hat c_{v,i}$,
$\hat c_{p,i}$ [-] for the dimensionless forms the code stores; $u^\star_i$ the energy offset at the reference state of
@sec-ch03-reference-state; $U, H, C_V, C_p$ the per-volume totals [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$,
$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$]; $T_0 = 300\,\mathrm K$ the junction temperature of the opt-in models (`kNasa9Tref`);
$\theta_{\mathrm{rot}} = 87.55\,\mathrm K$ the rotational temperature of $\mathrm{H_2}$ (`kThetaRot`);
$a_0, \dots, a_7$ the NASA-9 coefficients of one temperature range. The internal names are `eval_cv_R`, `eval_cp_R`,
`eval_intEng_R`, `eval_enthalpy_R`; the options are `use_nasa9_cp`, `use_h2_cp`, `h2_cp_mode`.

### Derivation

**The baseline.** With a constant heat capacity $\hat c_{v,i}$ (`cref_R`, from the card's `cv_R`) and the offset
$u^\star_i$ stored at $T = 0$ (@sec-ch03-reference-state), the molar internal energy of every species is
$$
\hat u_i(T) = \frac{u^\star_i}{\mathcal R} + \hat c_{v,i}\,T + \hat e_i(T, c_i), \qquad
\hat c_{v,i}(T) = \hat c_{v,i} + \partial_T \hat e_i ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-u-baseline}
where $\hat e_i$ is an optional extra function named per species in `intEng_R_extra` (its derivative is the function of
the same name with `_ddT` appended). @eq-ch03-caloric-u-baseline is computed in `eval_intEng_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_intEng_R >}}) and its derivative in `eval_cv_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_cv_R >}}). At the pin the extra-function registry is
empty (@sec-ch03-eos), so $\hat e_i = 0$ and the baseline is the straight line of @fig-ch03-reference-state-offsets. The
heat capacity at constant pressure adds $\mathcal R$ for a gas and nothing for a condensate (the Mayer relation of an
ideal gas; an incompressible condensate has $c_p = c_v$),
$$
\hat c_{p,i} = \hat c_{v,i} + 1 \quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}), \qquad \hat c_{p,i} = \hat c_{v,i} \quad (i \ge N_{\mathrm g}),
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-cp}
and @eq-ch03-caloric-cp is computed in `eval_cp_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_cp_R >}}) (`[C5]` of
`caloric_check.py`). The enthalpy follows as $h = u + p/c$ for a gas, which with the equation of state of
@sec-ch03-eos is $u + z_i \mathcal R T$, and as $h = u$ plus an optional extra for a condensate:
$$
\hat h_i = \hat u_i + z_i\,T \quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}), \qquad \hat h_i = \hat u_i + \hat e^{h}_i \quad (i \ge N_{\mathrm g}),
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-h}
computed in `eval_enthalpy_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_enthalpy_R >}}); the condensate extra
$\hat e^{h}_i$ shares the `czh` slot of the species record with the gas compressibility, and is zero at the pin.

**The NASA-9 polynomial** (`use-nasa9-cp`). For a species with a record in `data/nasa9.dat`, two ranges of
coefficients (below and above a mid-point temperature) give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat c_{p,i}(T) &= \frac{a_0}{T^2} + \frac{a_1}{T} + a_2 + a_3 T + a_4 T^2 + a_5 T^3 + a_6 T^4, \\
\hat h_i(T) &= -\frac{a_0}{T} + a_1 \ln T + a_2 T + \frac{a_3 T^2}{2} + \frac{a_4 T^3}{3} + \frac{a_5 T^4}{4} + \frac{a_6 T^5}{5} + a_7 ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-nasa9}
with $\mathrm d\hat h_i/\mathrm dT = \hat c_{p,i}$ (`[C1]`). @eq-ch03-caloric-nasa9 is computed in `nasa9_cp_R` and
`nasa9_h_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp nasa9_h_R >}}). The model is used for $c_p$, $c_v = c_p - \mathcal R$
and the energy, but *not* for the entropy, which stays on the baseline. To keep the energy continuous with the
baseline and with the offsets of @sec-ch03-reference-state, the internal energy is referenced to $T_0$:
$$
\hat u_i(T) = \frac{u^\star_i}{\mathcal R} + \hat c_{v,i}\,T_0 + \bigl[\hat h_i(T) - \hat h_i(T_0)\bigr] - (T - T_0),
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-nasa9-u}
so that $\hat u_i(T_0)$ is the baseline value and $\mathrm d\hat u_i/\mathrm dT = \hat c_{p,i} - 1$ (`[C2]`).
@eq-ch03-caloric-nasa9-u is computed in `eval_nasa9` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_nasa9 >}}), which also
builds the mask of species that carry a record; species without one stay on the baseline exactly.

**The hydrogen rotor** (`use-h2-cp`). For the species named `H2` the rotational partition function of a rigid rotor
with levels $\varepsilon_J = \theta_{\mathrm{rot}}\,m_J\,k_{\mathrm B}$, $m_J = J(J+1)$, summed to $J = 40$, gives the
mean $\langle m \rangle$ and the rotational heat capacity
$$
\langle m \rangle = \frac{\sum_J w_J\, m_J\, e^{-\theta_{\mathrm{rot}} m_J/T}}{\sum_J w_J\, e^{-\theta_{\mathrm{rot}} m_J/T}}, \qquad
\hat c_{v,\mathrm{rot}} = \Bigl(\frac{\theta_{\mathrm{rot}}}{T}\Bigr)^2 \bigl(\langle m^2 \rangle - \langle m \rangle^2\bigr),
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-h2-rot}
with weights $w_J = 2J+1$ times the nuclear-spin factor: in `equilibrium` mode one Boltzmann ensemble with weight
$3$ on odd $J$ (ortho) and $1$ on even $J$ (para); in `normal` mode two separate ensembles mixed $1{:}3$ para to ortho,
so that no conversion heat appears. @eq-ch03-caloric-h2-rot is computed in `h2_rot_reduce`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp h2_rot_reduce >}}) and assembled in `eval_h2cp`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_h2cp >}}) as
$$
\hat c_{p} = \tfrac52 + \hat c_{v,\mathrm{rot}}, \qquad
\hat u(T) = \frac{u^\star}{\mathcal R} + \hat c_{v}\,T_0 + \tfrac32 (T - T_0) + \theta_{\mathrm{rot}}\bigl(\langle m \rangle(T) - \langle m \rangle(T_0)\bigr),
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-h2-u}
again continuous with the baseline at $T_0$ and with $\mathrm d\hat u/\mathrm dT = \hat c_p - 1$ (`[C4]`). The
rotor overrides the NASA-9 record for `H2` when both are on.

**Totals and the inversion.** The per-volume energy and heat capacity are the concentration-weighted sums,
$U = \mathcal R \sum_i c_i \hat u_i$ and $C_V = \mathcal R \sum_i c_i \hat c_{v,i}$, in
`ThermoYImpl::_intEng_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_vol >}}) and
`ThermoYImpl::_cv_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_cv_vol >}}); $C_p$ and $H$ likewise in
`ThermoXImpl::_cp_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_cp_vol >}}) and `ThermoXImpl::_enthalpy_vol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_enthalpy_vol >}}). Temperature from energy is the Newton iteration
$$
T \leftarrow T + \frac{U - \mathcal R\sum_i c_i \hat u_i(T)}{\mathcal R \sum_i c_i \hat c_{v,i}(T)}, \qquad
T^{(0)} = \frac{U - \sum_i \rho_i u^\star_i / M_i}{\sum_i \rho_i c_{v,i}/M_i},
$$ {#eq-ch03-caloric-newton-u}
whose starting guess is the exact answer of the baseline, so the loop again exits after one pass there;
@eq-ch03-caloric-newton-u is computed in `ThermoYImpl::_intEng_to_temp`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_to_temp >}}). With an opt-in model the iteration is a true
Newton method on a convex energy ($c_v > 0$) and stops on the relative change $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ of
@sec-ch03-eos.

What is exact: the baseline and both opt-in energies as functions of $T$, and the one-step inversion for the baseline.
What is truncated: the rotor sum at $J = 40$ (the omitted terms are below $e^{-40\cdot41\cdot 87.55/T}$, negligible
below $3000\,\mathrm K$); the NASA-9 fit outside its $200$ to $6000\,\mathrm K$ range is an extrapolation of the
polynomial, not data. The check is `caloric_check.py`, whose numbers appear in the Tests layer below.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch03-caloric-h2cp shows the three models for $\mathrm{H_2}$ against temperature. All three are point
evaluations per cell and species with no stencil; the rotor evaluates $41$ exponentials per cell, the polynomial
seven powers, and both select their branch (range, or ortho-para weights) with a mask so that species without the
model keep the baseline bit for bit. The energy-to-temperature loop of @eq-ch03-caloric-newton-u is the only
iteration, and it runs over all cells at once with the maximum relative change as its stopping test.

### Summary

The caloric data of a card are given at a reference state: `u0_R` is the internal energy over $\mathcal R$ of a
species at the reference temperature `Tref`, and `s0_R` its entropy over $\mathcal R$ at `Tref` and the reference
pressure `Pref`. The latent heat of a phase change is not a separate input; it is the difference of the `u0_R`
values of vapour and condensate, and it must be positive for condensation to release energy. This section explains
how the offsets are shifted once, at construction, to $T = 0$ and to $T = 1\,\mathrm K$, $p = 1\,\mathrm{Pa}$ so that
every later formula is offset-free, why the card is warned about an endothermic condensate, and how the offsets have
to agree with the saturation curve of @sec-ch04 through the Clausius-Clapeyron relation.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Fix $u^\star_i$ and $s^\star_i$ from the card, @eq-ch03-reference-state-shift, and the latent heat
$\ell_j = -\sum_i \nu_{ij} u^\star_i$ that follows.

**Data.** `reference-state: {Tref, Pref}` [K, Pa] and per species `u0_R` [K], `s0_R` [-], `cv_R` [-]; in memory
`uref_R`, `sref_R`, `cref_R` after the shift.

**Placement.** Once, in `ThermoY::reset` or `ThermoX::reset`; guarded by the flag `offset_zero` so a cloned options
object is not shifted twice.

**Activation.** Always; defaults `Tref` $300\,\mathrm K$, `Pref` $10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}$, `u0_R` $0$, `s0_R` $0$. An
unknown key in `reference-state` is refused with a suggestion.

**Guarantee / limits.** The shift leaves $u_i(T)$ and $s_i(T, p)$ unchanged (exact algebra); a latent heat
$\le 0$ at `Tref` only warns.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `test_latent_heat_sign.py`, `test_reference_state_keys.py`.
:::

Local symbols: $T_\star$ and $p_\star$ the reference temperature and pressure (`Tref`, `Pref`); $u^\star_i$ and
$s^\star_i$ the stored offsets (`uref_R`, `sref_R`, as $u^\star_i/\mathcal R$ in K and $s^\star_i/\mathcal R$);
$\nu_{ij}$ the stoichiometric coefficient of species $i$ in reaction $j$, positive for products (`stoich`);
$\ell_j$ the molar latent heat of reaction $j$ [$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$]; for the saturation curve the fit
parameters $\beta$, $\delta$, $T_r$, $p_r$ of the `ideal` form (@sec-ch04). The star marks the reference
state as the shared notation requires; the internal flag is `offset_zero`.

### Derivation

The card gives, per species, $\hat u_i(T_\star) =$ `u0_R` and $\hat s_i(T_\star, p_\star) =$ `s0_R` together with the
constant $\hat c_{v,i} =$ `cv_R`. With the baseline of @sec-ch03-caloric the energy at any temperature is
$\hat u_i(T) = \texttt{u0\_R} + \hat c_{v,i}(T - T_\star)$, and the entropy of a gas at any $(T, p)$ is
$\hat s_i = \texttt{s0\_R} + (\hat c_{v,i} + 1)\ln(T/T_\star) - \ln(p/p_\star)$. Collecting the constants gives the
offsets the code stores,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{u^\star_i}{\mathcal R} &= \texttt{u0\_R}_i - \hat c_{v,i}\,T_\star \quad \text{all species}, \\
\frac{s^\star_i}{\mathcal R} &= \texttt{s0\_R}_i - (\hat c_{v,i} + 1)\ln\max(T_\star, 1) + \ln\max(p_\star, 1) \quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}), \\
\frac{s^\star_i}{\mathcal R} &= 0 \quad (i \ge N_{\mathrm g}),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-reference-state-shift}
after which $\hat u_i(T) = u^\star_i/\mathcal R + \hat c_{v,i} T$ and $\hat s_i = s^\star_i/\mathcal R + (\hat c_{v,i}+1)\ln T - \ln p$
are the same functions as before (`[C1]`, `[C2]` of `reference_state_check.py`). @eq-ch03-reference-state-shift is
computed in `ThermoYImpl::reset` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}) and identically in
`ThermoXImpl::reset` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::reset >}}). The clamps to $1$ let a card say
`Tref: 0.` (several test cards do) and mean "the offsets are already at $T = 0$", because $\ln 1 = 0$. The condensate
entropy offsets are set to zero because @sec-ch03-entropy derives the condensate entropy from the saturation curve
and never reads them. The flag `offset_zero` records that the shift has happened, so an options object shared by a
`ThermoX` and a `ThermoY`, or cloned, is shifted once.

The latent heat of reaction $j$ at the reference temperature is the energy released when the reaction proceeds by
one mole of extent, $\ell_j(T_\star) = -\mathcal R\sum_i \nu_{ij}\,\texttt{u0\_R}_i$, since $\nu_{ij} < 0$ for the
vapour consumed and $> 0$ for the condensate formed. The card loader evaluates this sum for every nucleation
reaction and warns when it is not positive:
$$
\ell_j(T_\star) = \mathcal R \Bigl(\sum_{i\,\in\,\mathrm{reactants}} |\nu_{ij}|\,\texttt{u0\_R}_i - \sum_{i\,\in\,\mathrm{products}} \nu_{ij}\,\texttt{u0\_R}_i\Bigr) \le 0
\;\Rightarrow\; \text{warning},
$$ {#eq-ch03-reference-state-latent}
and @eq-ch03-reference-state-latent is computed in `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}). For `tests/jupiter.yaml`,
$\mathrm{H_2O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H_2O(l)}$ has $\texttt{u0\_R} = 0$ and $-3430\,\mathrm K$, so
$\ell/\mathcal R = 3430\,\mathrm K$ ($28.5\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$); a condensate without `u0_R` gives $0$ and the
warning (`[C3]`).

The offsets are not free: they must agree with the saturation curve that @sec-ch04 uses, or the energy released by
condensation in the fixed-energy solver will not match the temperature dependence of the curve. For the `ideal`
curve $\ln p_{\mathrm{sat}} = \ln p_r + \beta(1 - T_r/T) - \delta\ln(T/T_r)$ and an ideal vapour over a condensate of
negligible volume, the Clausius-Clapeyron relation $\ell = \mathcal R T^2\,\mathrm d\ln p_{\mathrm{sat}}/\mathrm dT$ gives
$$
\ell(T) = \mathcal R\,(\beta T_r - \delta T),
$$ {#eq-ch03-reference-state-kirchhoff}
linear in $T$ with slope $-\mathcal R\delta = c_{p,v} - c_{c}$: the Kirchhoff form (`[C4]`). With the baseline
enthalpies $\hat h_v - \hat h_c = (u^\star_v - u^\star_c)/\mathcal R + (\hat c_{v,v} + 1 - \hat c_{v,c})\,T$, a
consistent card therefore has $\delta = \hat c_{v,c} - \hat c_{v,v} - 1$ and $\beta T_r = (u^\star_v - u^\star_c)/\mathcal R$.
The Jupiter test card uses the `h2o_ideal` constants ($\beta = 24.845$, $T_r = 273.16\,\mathrm K$, $\delta = 4.986$)
with $\hat c_{v,c} - \hat c_{v,v} - 1 = 9 - 2.5 - 1 = 5.5$ and $(u^\star_v - u^\star_c)/\mathcal R = 5380\,\mathrm K$
against $\beta T_r = 6787\,\mathrm K$: it is *not* Kirchhoff-consistent, and its moist adiabats carry that
inconsistency (@sec-ch03-adiabat). Two cards in the tree are consistent by construction: `h2o_bryan`, whose $\beta$
is chosen so that $\ell(273.15\,\mathrm K) = 2.5\times10^6\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$ (`[C5]`, reproducing the literal
$24.815845$ of {{< code src/vapors/vapor_functions.h h2o_bryan >}}), and `examples/jupiter_kcl_mgsio3.yaml`, whose
`u0_R` values are $-B\ln 10$ for curves of the form $\ln(10)(A - B/T)$ with $\Delta c_p = 0$ (`[C6]`). The check
`reference_state_check.py` holds all six statements.

### Numerical method

There is no discretisation in this section; @fig-ch03-reference-state-offsets shows what the shift does to the two
energy lines of water in the Jupiter card. The order of operations at construction is: read the card, form the
species groups (@sec-ch03-species-state), copy `cv_R`, `u0_R`, `s0_R` into `cref_R`, `uref_R`, `sref_R` in group
order, then shift once in `reset`. A `ThermoY` and a `ThermoX` built from the same options object share the shifted
arrays. The latent-heat sum is evaluated on the *unshifted* `u0_R`, which is the same as on the shifted $u^\star_i$
only when the heat capacities of vapour and condensate are equal; the warning therefore tests the latent heat at
$T_\star$, as its message says.

### Summary

The entropy is what the adiabat routines of @sec-ch03-adiabat conserve and what a host code uses to place a
parcel on an adiabat, so it has to be consistent with the energies of @sec-ch03-caloric and with the saturation
curves of @sec-ch04. For a gas kintera uses the ideal-gas entropy at the species' partial pressure. For a
condensate it does not use a card value at all: it derives the condensate entropy from the condition that the
Gibbs energy change of each phase-change reaction vanishes on its saturation curve, which makes the entropy
consistent with the saturation curve by construction. This section gives both formulas, the pseudo-inverse that
solves the condensate system, and the inversion from entropy to temperature that `ThermoX` offers.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $s_i(T, p, x)$ per species, @eq-ch03-entropy-gas and @eq-ch03-entropy-condensate, and the per-volume
$S = \sum_i c_i s_i$; the Gibbs energy $G = H - TS$ and the Helmholtz energy $F = U - TS$.

**Data.** In: $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], concentrations $c_i$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] (or partial densities); out:
$S$ [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$], $G$ and $F$ [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$].

**Placement.** `compute` keys `PVT->S` (`ThermoY`), `TPV->S`, `PXS->T`, `THS->G` (`ThermoX`), `TUS->F` (`ThermoY`);
inside `extrapolate_dlnp` and `extrapolate_dz`.

**Activation.** Always; the condensate branch needs the nucleation reactions of the card (@sec-ch04). With
no reactions `TPV->S` is the gas formula alone.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact for ideal gases with constant heat capacities; the condensate entropy is exact when each
condensate appears in one reaction and a minimum-norm solution otherwise. The entropy ignores the opt-in heat
capacities of @sec-ch03-caloric.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `DeviceTest.thermo_x` closes `PXS->T` to $10^{-4}$; `test_thermo_none_nucleation.py`.
:::

Local symbols: $L_j(T) = \ln Q_j^{\mathrm{sat}}$ the logarithm of the saturation quotient of reaction $j$ (the
`logsvp` function of the card; defined in @sec-ch04); $a_{ij} = -\nu_{ij}$ for a gas reactant;
$\mathsf S^{+}$ the condensate block of the stoichiometric matrix ($N_{\mathrm c} \times N_{\mathrm r}$, `sp`);
$b_j$ the right-hand side of the condensate system; $N_{\mathrm r}$ the number of nucleation reactions. The energy
and reference symbols are those of @sec-ch03-caloric and @sec-ch03-reference-state.

### Derivation

**Gases.** An ideal gas with constant heat capacity at its partial pressure $p_i = p\,x_i/x_{\mathrm g}$ has
$$
\hat s_i = \frac{s^\star_i}{\mathcal R} + \hat c_{p,i}\ln T - \ln p - \ln\frac{c_i}{c_{\mathrm g}} + \hat e^{s}_i
\quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}),
$$ {#eq-ch03-entropy-gas}
where $c_i/c_{\mathrm g} = x_i/x_{\mathrm g}$ is the gas-only mole fraction, clamped below at $10^{-300}$ before the
logarithm so that an absent gas gives a large finite entropy instead of infinity, and $\hat e^{s}_i$ is the optional
`entropy_R_extra` hook (none registered at the pin). @eq-ch03-entropy-gas is computed in the two overloads of
`eval_entropy_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_entropy_R overload=2 >}}); the first overload, taking the
species record alone, evaluates only this gas part. That $-\ln p - \ln(x_i/x_{\mathrm g}) = -\ln p_i$ is `[C1]` of
`entropy_check.py`.

**Condensates.** On the saturation curve of reaction $j$ the Gibbs energy change vanishes, $\sum_i \nu_{ij} g_i = 0$
with $g_i = h_i - T s_i$. Splitting the sum into gases and condensates and solving for the condensate part,
$$
\sum_{i \ge N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{ij}\,\hat s_i
= \frac{1}{T}\sum_{i} \nu_{ij}\,\hat h_i - \sum_{i < N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{ij}\,\hat s_i .
$$
The gas entropies on the right are those of @eq-ch03-entropy-gas evaluated *on the saturation curve*, where
$\sum_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} a_{ij}\ln p_i = L_j(T)$ (@sec-ch04), so that
$-\sum_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{ij}\ln p_i = L_j$ and the partial pressures drop out:
$$
b_j \equiv \sum_{i \ge N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{ij}\,\hat s_i
= \frac{1}{T}\sum_{i} \nu_{ij}\,\hat h_i - \sum_{i < N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{ij}\Bigl(\frac{s^\star_i}{\mathcal R} + \hat c_{p,i}\ln T + \hat e^{s}_i\Bigr) - L_j(T) .
$$ {#eq-ch03-entropy-b}
@eq-ch03-entropy-b is computed in `eval_entropy_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_entropy_R overload=2 >}}),
which evaluates $L_j$ through `LogSVPFunc::call` ({{< code src/thermo/log_svp.hpp LogSVPFunc::call >}}) and the
enthalpies through `eval_enthalpy_R` of @sec-ch03-caloric (`[C2]`). The condensate entropies are then the solution
of the linear system $(\mathsf S^{+})^{\mathrm T}\,\hat{\mathbf s}_{\mathrm c} = \mathbf b$,
$$
\hat{\mathbf s}_{\mathrm c} = \bigl[(\mathsf S^{+})^{\mathrm T}\bigr]^{+}\,\mathbf b ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-entropy-condensate}
with the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse $[\cdot]^+$, computed in the same `eval_entropy_R` through `torch.linalg.pinv`.
When every condensate is the product of exactly one reaction with coefficient one, as in `tests/jupiter.yaml`,
$\mathsf S^{+}$ is a permutation of the identity and $\hat s_{\mathrm c,i} = b_j$ exactly; when a condensate appears
in several reactions, or several condensates share one, the pseudo-inverse returns the least-squares, minimum-norm
solution (`[C3]`). The condensate's own `s0_R` never enters, which is why @sec-ch03-reference-state zeroes it.

The construction makes the entropy consistent with the saturation curve whatever the card's offsets: by
@eq-ch03-entropy-b the gap $T(s_v - s_c)$ between a vapour at its saturation partial pressure and its condensate
equals $h_v - h_c$ exactly, which @fig-ch03-entropy-condensate shows for water. Whether that $h_v - h_c$ is the
latent heat the saturation curve implies is the Kirchhoff question of @sec-ch03-reference-state.

**Free energies and the inversion.** The per-volume totals are $S = \mathcal R\sum_i c_i \hat s_i$ in
`ThermoYImpl::_entropy_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl::_entropy_vol >}}) and
`ThermoXImpl::_entropy_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_entropy_vol >}}), then $G = H - TS$
(`THS->G`) and $F = U - TS$ (`TUS->F`) in the `compute` dispatch. Temperature from a target entropy at fixed pressure
and mole fractions is the iteration
$$
T \leftarrow T\Bigl(1 + \frac{S_{\mathrm{target}} - S(T)}{C_p(T)}\Bigr), \qquad T^{(0)} = T_\star,
$$ {#eq-ch03-entropy-newton}
followed in each pass by a saturation adjustment of the mole fractions at the new temperature (`forward`,
@sec-ch04), so that the entropy target is met on the equilibrium composition.
@eq-ch03-entropy-newton is computed in `ThermoXImpl::_entropy_to_temp`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_entropy_to_temp >}}). It is the Newton step on
$S(T) - S_{\mathrm{target}}$ with $\partial S/\partial T = C_p/T$ at fixed pressure, linearised in $T$ (the same
form as the adiabat update of @sec-ch03-adiabat, whose check `adiabat_check.py` `[C4]` gives its remainder).

Exact: the gas entropy, and the condensate entropy for one-to-one reaction blocks. Approximate: the minimum-norm
split for shared condensates has no thermodynamic meaning beyond reproducing $b_j$; the iteration
@eq-ch03-entropy-newton is first order in its step and stops on the relative change of $T$.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch03-entropy-condensate shows the two entropies of water over temperature and the identity that the
construction enforces. The condensate solve is one `pinv` of an $N_{\mathrm r} \times N_{\mathrm c}$ matrix that
depends only on the stoichiometry, broadcast over all cells, followed by one matrix-vector product per cell; the
matrix is small (three by three for the Jupiter card) and the cost is in the $L_j(T)$ and enthalpy evaluations. The
`PXS->T` loop starts every cell at $T_\star$ (not at the previous temperature), calls the full saturation solver
once per pass, and stops on the maximum relative change over all cells; after `max-iter` passes it warns and writes
the inputs to a time-stamped `.pt` file, as `TPX->V` does (@sec-ch03-eos).

### Summary

The saturation ratio of a phase-change reaction is the quotient of its gas partial pressures divided by the
equilibrium quotient at the same temperature: above one the gases are supersaturated and the condensate forms,
below one the condensate evaporates. For a single vapour condensing to a pure phase it is the relative humidity of
meteorology, which gives the function its name; kintera's version handles any reaction of the nucleation type,
including products of several partial pressures (ammonium hydrosulfide) and reactions with a gaseous product. It is
a diagnostic, evaluated after a saturation adjustment to check how close each reaction is to equilibrium; the
solvers of @sec-ch04 use the same quotient internally, in logarithmic form.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\varphi_j = Q_j / Q_j^{\mathrm{sat}}(T)$ per reaction, @eq-ch03-relative-humidity-ratio.

**Data.** In: $T$ [K], concentrations $c_i$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$], the stoichiometric matrix, the nucleation
options and, for cards with gaseous products, the number of gases; out: $\varphi_j$ [-], shape $(\dots, N_{\mathrm r})$.

**Placement.** A free function (`kintera.relative_humidity`), called by the examples and tests after `forward`.

**Activation.** Always available; the argument `ngas` defaults to $-1$ (legacy: all reactants, condensates
included at unit activity) and must be given when a reaction has a gaseous product, or the call raises.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact algebra on the ideal-gas partial pressures; zero amounts give $0$, $\infty$ or
`nan`, never an exception.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `test_antoine_equilibrate_tp_saturates` holds
$|\varphi - 1| < 10^{-8}$ in cloudy cells.
:::

Local symbols: $\varphi_j$ the saturation ratio of reaction $j$ [-]; $Q_j = \prod_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} p_i^{a_{ij}}$ its
gas-pressure quotient in Pa to the power $A_j$; $A_j = \sum_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} a_{ij}$ the net number of gas moles
consumed; $L_j(T) = \ln Q_j^{\mathrm{sat}}$ as in @sec-ch03-entropy. The name `relative_humidity` is kept in the
heading because it is the API name; the quantity is a saturation ratio.

### Derivation

With $p_i = c_i\mathcal R T$ for each gas and unit activity for every pure condensate, the quotient of reaction $j$
over its saturation value is
$$
\varphi_j = \frac{\prod_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} (c_i \mathcal R T)^{a_{ij}}}{\exp L_j(T)}
= \frac{\prod_{i<N_{\mathrm g}} c_i^{a_{ij}}}{\exp\bigl(L_j(T) - A_j \ln(\mathcal R T)\bigr)} ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-relative-humidity-ratio}
and the second form, which moves the $(\mathcal R T)^{A_j}$ into the denominator, is what the code evaluates:
@eq-ch03-relative-humidity-ratio is computed in `relative_humidity`
({{< code src/thermo/relative_humidity.cpp relative_humidity >}}) with $L_j$ from `LogSVPFunc::call`
({{< code src/thermo/log_svp.hpp LogSVPFunc::call >}}). The equivalence of the two forms is `[C1]` of
`relative_humidity_check.py`. For $\mathrm{NH_3 + H_2S \rightleftharpoons NH_4SH(s)}$, $a = 1$ for both gases and
$A_j = 2$, so $\varphi$ is a product of two partial pressures over a constant with the units of $\mathrm{Pa^2}$, which
is why $L_j$ must be stated in Pa (@sec-ch04).

The exponent matrix is where the gaseous products matter. Without `ngas` the code takes $a_{ij} = |\min(\nu_{ij}, 0)|$
over *all* species: every reactant, which is right only when all products are condensates (unit activity) and is
the legacy meaning of the function. With `ngas` it takes $a_{ij} = -\nu_{ij}$ over the first `ngas` rows and zero
below, so that a gaseous product such as $\mathrm{H_2}$ in $\mathrm{Mn + H_2S \rightleftharpoons MnS(s) + H_2}$ enters
with exponent $-1$ (`[C2]`). The function refuses the legacy call for options whose builder has recorded a gaseous
product (`has_gas_products`, set by `add_to_vapor_cloud` in @sec-ch03-species-state), with the message
`relative_humidity requires ngas for gaseous reaction products`.

Zero amounts are not special-cased: a zero reactant concentration makes $\varphi_j = 0$, a zero gaseous product makes
it infinite, and both at once make it `nan` (`[C4]`); the solvers of @sec-ch04 treat the last case as a blocked
reaction rather than evaluating the quotient. Nothing is truncated: the relation is exact for ideal gases, and the
check `relative_humidity_check.py` holds it symbolically and on a water example (`[C3]`: $1\,\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$ of
water vapour at $300\,\mathrm K$ has $\varphi = 0.7047$ against the `h2o_ideal` curve, whose saturation pressure there
is $3539.5\,\mathrm{Pa}$).

### Numerical method

The evaluation is element-wise over cells and reactions: one `LogSVPFunc::call` for all reactions (the same
vectorised evaluation @sec-ch03-entropy uses), one broadcast power and product over the species axis, one
exponential. @fig-ch03-relative-humidity-quotient shows the ratio for two reactions at fixed gas concentrations
across temperature; the slope of each curve on the logarithmic axis is $-\mathrm dL_j/\mathrm dT + A_j/T$, which is
the temperature sensitivity the fixed-energy solver of @sec-ch04 linearises. There is no tolerance
and no iteration.

### Summary

A parcel that rises adiabatically cools, and when it is saturated part of the cooling is offset by the latent heat of
the condensate it forms. kintera builds such a profile one step at a time: given an equilibrated state at one
pressure (or height), `ThermoX` finds the temperature at the next pressure that conserves the parcel's molar
entropy, equilibrating the phases at every trial temperature. The Newton step of that search needs the derivative
of entropy with respect to temperature *along the saturation curve*, which is the frozen heat capacity plus a
latent term; that sum is the effective heat capacity, and the latent term is read off the gain matrix that the
saturation solver of @sec-ch04 returns. An option drops the condensate after each step for a
pseudo-adiabat. This is the moist adiabat with several condensing species of Li, Ingersoll and Oyafuso
([J. Atmos. Sci. 75, 1063, 2018](https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS-D-17-0257.1)), written for an arbitrary set of
nucleation reactions, with the entropy of @sec-ch03-entropy as its conserved quantity.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Step $(T, p, x)$ along an adiabat by $\Delta\ln p$ or $\Delta z$, conserving molar entropy;
the effective heat capacity is @eq-ch03-adiabat-cp-eff.

**Data.** In and out, in place: $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], mole fractions $x_i$ of all species; parameters
$\Delta\ln p$ or $\Delta z$ [m] with $g$ [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$]; optional entropy source per step.

**Placement.** `ThermoX.extrapolate_dlnp` and `ThermoX.extrapolate_dz`; `ThermoX.effective_cp` on its own after
any `forward`.

**Activation.** Called explicitly by a host or script; `rainout` (default off) drops the condensates after each step;
`ds_dlnp` or `ds_dz` (default 0) adds an entropy source; `max-iter` and `ftol` of the card bound the search.

**Guarantee / limits.** Entropy conserved to $10\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ per step (the stopping test); first-order
accurate in the step size; `dz` steps iterate hydrostatic balance with the mean density of the step.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad` (entropy to $10^{-3}$), the deep-Jupiter example
(entropy to $10^{-5}\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, dry limit to $10^{-5}\,\mathrm K$).
:::

Local symbols: $s$ the molar entropy of the parcel, all species counted [$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$]
($S/\sum_i c_i$); $\xi_j$ the extent of reaction $j$ per mole of parcel [-]; $\mathsf G$ the gain matrix of the
saturation solver, $G_{jk} = \partial r_j/\partial \xi_k$ with $r_j$ the saturation residual of @sec-ch04
(`gain`); $L'_j = \mathrm dL_j/\mathrm dT$; $c_{p}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ the effective molar heat capacity
[$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$]; $g$ the gravitational acceleration, positive downward [$\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$];
$\bar M = \sum_i x_i M_i$ the mean molar mass. The internal names are `effective_cp`, `extrapolate_dlnp`,
`extrapolate_dz`; the options object is `ExtrapOptions`.

### Derivation

**The effective heat capacity.** At fixed pressure, along the saturation curve, the parcel's enthalpy changes with
temperature both through the heat capacities and through the extents of the phase changes:
$$
\frac{\mathrm dH}{\mathrm dT}\Bigr|_{p,\,\mathrm{sat}} = \sum_i x_i c_{p,i} + \sum_j \Bigl(\sum_i h_i \nu_{ij}\Bigr)\frac{\mathrm d\xi_j}{\mathrm dT} .
$$
The extents follow the saturation conditions $r_j(T, \boldsymbol\xi) = 0$ of the active
reactions (@sec-ch04). Differentiating along the curve, $\sum_k G_{jk}\,\mathrm d\xi_k/\mathrm dT = \partial r_j/\partial T$,
and since $r_j$ depends on $T$ only through $-L_j(T)$, the right-hand side is $L'_j(T)$ up to the sign convention of
the solver's gain matrix. kintera therefore solves the linear system
$$
\mathsf G\,\frac{\mathrm d\boldsymbol\xi}{\mathrm dT} = \mathbf L', \qquad
c_p^{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_i x_i\,c_{p,i} + \sum_j \Bigl(\sum_i h_i \nu_{ij}\Bigr)\frac{\mathrm d\xi_j}{\mathrm dT},
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-cp-eff}
where $\mathsf G$ is the gain matrix returned by the last `forward`, zero outside the active reactions.
@eq-ch03-adiabat-cp-eff is computed in `ThermoXImpl::effective_cp`
({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::effective_cp >}}), with $L'_j$ from `LogSVPFunc::grad`
({{< code src/thermo/log_svp.hpp LogSVPFunc::grad >}}) and $h_i$, $c_{p,i}$ from @sec-ch03-caloric. For one vapour
condensing in a carrier gas the gain is the scalar $G = 1/x_{\mathrm g} - 1/x_v$ (`[C1]` of `adiabat_check.py`),
$\sum_i h_i\nu_{ij} = h_c - h_v = -\ell$, and the latent term becomes
$$
c_p^{\mathrm{latent}} = \ell\,L'\,\frac{x_v x_{\mathrm g}}{x_{\mathrm g} - x_v}
\;\xrightarrow{\;x_v \ll x_{\mathrm g}\;}\; x_v\,\frac{\ell^2}{\mathcal R T^2},
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-latent-single}
using $L' = \ell/(\mathcal R T^2)$ for an ideal vapour: the classical moist correction (`[C2]`). For the water case
of @fig-ch03-adiabat-effective-cp at $290\,\mathrm K$ and $1\,\mathrm{bar}$ the latent term is $1.3$ times the frozen
heat capacity (`[C3]`).

The linear solve is ill-conditioned when one active reaction involves a nearly depleted vapour: that reaction's row
of $\mathsf G$ is scaled by $1/x_v$ and can be $10^{12}$ times larger than the row that carries the latent heat, and a
least-squares solver with a relative rank tolerance drops exactly the small row. The code therefore divides each
row of $\mathsf G$ and the matching entry of $\mathbf L'$ by the row's largest magnitude before the solve (the same
solution in exact arithmetic, condition number of order one), solves with the `gelsd` driver on CPU (whose pivoting,
unlike the default driver's, does not depend on uninitialised memory) and with a pseudo-inverse of absolute tolerance
$10^{-6}$ on CUDA; a zero row (inactive reaction) keeps scale one and a zero rate.

**Stepping in pressure.** The parcel's molar entropy $s_0$ at the start is the target. After multiplying the pressure
by $e^{\Delta\ln p}$, each pass restores the starting composition, equilibrates it at the current $T$
(`forward`, which also returns $\mathsf G$), evaluates $s(T)$ and $c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}$, and updates
$$
T \leftarrow T\Bigl(1 + \frac{s_{\mathrm{target}} - s(T)}{c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\Bigr), \qquad
s_{\mathrm{target}} = s_0 + \frac{\mathrm ds}{\mathrm d\ln p}\,\Delta\ln p ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-newton}
until $|s_{\mathrm{target}} - s(T)| < 10\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ (in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, an absolute
test) or `max-iter` passes. @eq-ch03-adiabat-newton is computed in `ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp`
({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp >}}). It is the Newton step on
$s(T) - s_{\mathrm{target}}$ with $\partial s/\partial T|_{p,\mathrm{sat}} = c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}/T$, linearised in $T$
instead of $\ln T$; the remainder of one step is $c_p\,\delta^2/2$ with $\delta = (s_{\mathrm{target}} - s)/c_p$,
so the convergence is quadratic (`[C4]`). With `rainout` the condensates are removed from the composition after
each equilibration and the target is reduced by the entropy they carry away, per mole of gas,
$$
s_{\mathrm{target}} = \frac{x_{\mathrm{dry}}}{x_{\mathrm{dry},0}}\,s_0 - \frac{\sum_{i \ge N_{\mathrm g}} s_i c_i}{c_{\mathrm g}} + \frac{\mathrm ds}{\mathrm d\ln p}\,\Delta\ln p ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-rainout}
where the first factor rescales the starting entropy to the moles of (conserved) dry gas and the condensate
entropies $s_i$ are those of @sec-ch03-entropy; @eq-ch03-adiabat-rainout is computed in the same
`extrapolate_dlnp` (`[C5]`).

**Stepping in height.** `extrapolate_dz` ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dz >}})
takes the same Newton step with two additions: the pressure at the new height is not known in advance, so it starts
from the isothermal guess $p_0\exp(-g\bar M\Delta z/\mathcal R T)$ and in each pass re-evaluates hydrostatic balance
with the mean of the start and current densities,
$$
p \leftarrow p_0 - \tfrac12(\rho + \rho_0)\,g\,\Delta z, \qquad
T \leftarrow T\Bigl(1 + \frac{s_{\mathrm{target}} - s + x_{\mathrm g}\mathcal R\,\Delta\ln p}{c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\Bigr),
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-dz}
where $\Delta\ln p$ is the change of $\ln p$ within the pass and the term $x_{\mathrm g}\mathcal R\,\Delta\ln p$ is the
entropy change of the gas moles that the pressure update itself causes. @eq-ch03-adiabat-dz is computed in
`ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dz`. The hydrostatic update is the trapezoidal rule in $z$ with one Picard iteration per
Newton pass.

What is exact: the entropy conservation at convergence, to the stopping tolerance. What is truncated: the step is
first-order accurate in $\Delta\ln p$ or $\Delta z$ (the entropy is conserved at the end point, but the composition
that enters the latent heat is equilibrated at the end point only); the effective heat capacity is exact for the
linearised saturation conditions. The executable check is `adiabat_check.py` (`[C1]` to `[C5]`).

### Numerical method

Each step is an outer loop of at most `max-iter` passes over all cells at once. One pass is: restore $x$ to the
start of the step; `forward` at $(T, p)$, which returns $\mathsf G$; optionally drop the condensates and
renormalise; `TPX->V`, `effective_cp`, `TPV->S`; the convergence test on $\max_{\mathrm{cells}}|s_{\mathrm{target}} - s|$;
the temperature update. The `dz` variant inserts the pressure update before the temperature update.
@fig-ch03-adiabat-effective-cp shows the frozen and effective heat capacities of a water-saturated parcel of air and
the resulting dry and moist lapse rates $\mathrm d\ln T/\mathrm d\ln p = x_{\mathrm g}\mathcal R/c_p$. For the Jupiter
test card and $\Delta\ln p = -0.1$ at $200\,\mathrm K$, `DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad` runs with `max-iter` 15 and
`ftol` $10^{-8}$; the deep-Jupiter example instead calls `forward` inside its own bisection on specific entropy
(`run_column`, {{< code examples/example_jupiter_adiabat.py run_column >}}), because it needs entropy per unit mass
rather than per mole when the $\mathrm{MgSiO_3}$ reaction changes the number of molecules.
